title: Seasonal climate forecasts support advance prediction of European West Nile outbreaks
summary: An XGBoost model combined seasonal climate forecasts with past human-case and environmental data to estimate annual West Nile outbreak occurrence in Greece and 887 regions across 14 European countries. In held-out European years 2022–2024, it identified 81 of 91 first-recorded outbreaks in regions unaffected during training. This was an out-of-time evaluation of surveillance data, with variable false alarms and a marked decline in Greek municipal performance in 2025; it does not establish improved public-health outcomes.
ai_technology: XGBoost gradient-boosted classification; SHAP, SAGE and ALE interpretation

evidence.tested: Models trained on 2010–2021 were tested on later years (Greece 2022–2025; Europe 2022–2024). Rolling-origin development used earlier years only for preprocessing, feature selection and threshold setting. The European model identified 81/91 first-recorded regional outbreaks; Greek municipal AUCs were 0.94, 0.96, 0.92 and 0.74 across the four test years.
evidence.unknown: Out-of-time evaluation is not evidence that a frozen model was deployed prospectively. Forecast skill and false alarms varied by region/year; Greece deteriorated in 2025. Reporting/surveillance intensity differed across countries, and entomological or near-real-time data were unavailable. Mechanistic causation and public-health benefit were not tested.
evidence.ai_role: XGBoost learns an annual region-level outbreak classifier from pre-season climate forecasts and historical/environmental predictors. SHAP, SAGE and ALE describe learned predictive contributions rather than causal drivers.

source_review.scope: Original full-text source: abstract, publication metadata, relevant model/feature selection and validation Methods, Results and limitations. Supplementary files not assessed.
